title: Majorana physics in a Luttinger liquid with attractive interactions
authors: Francesco Debortoli, Nitya Cuzzuol, Luca Barbiero, Fabian Grusdt
abstract: Majorana zero modes are the hallmark of topological superconductivity. In one-dimensional systems, these zero modes are usually introduced in the context of gapped, mean-field models that do not conserve particle number, such as the Kitaev chain. By non-locally encoding a conventional fermion across spatially separated Majorana zero modes, these systems become inherently immune to local decoherence. In this work, we show that signatures of Majorana edge physics persist in a number-conserving, gapless Luttinger liquid of spinless fermions with short-range attractive interactions. We identify the two-point correlator as a sharp diagnostic, revealing an edge-to-edge revival whose sign depends on the fermion-number parity. This revival is robust in the thermodynamic limit, and persists in the excited states of the system and at different fillings. A simple particle-hole ansatz for the ground state of the system with an odd number of fermions captures the physics of the system for a wide range of interaction strengths, interpolating between the free-fermion limit and the strongly interacting Majorana regime. Finally, we propose a concrete protocol to realize this model with ultracold dipolar molecules or atoms in an optical lattice, and to detect the revival via beam-splitter interferometry, opening an experimental route to Majorana physics beyond the conventional gapped-superconductor paradigm.
summary: This paper shows that Majorana-like edge physics can exist in gapless Luttinger liquids of spinless fermions with attractive interactions. The key diagnostic is a robust 'edge-to-edge revival' in the two-point correlator, which survives even when moving to excited states. The authors propose realizing and detecting this phenomenon using ultracold dipolar atoms in an optical lattice.
main_problem: The work demonstrates that signatures of Majorana edge physics can persist in a number-conserving, gapless Luttinger liquid, contrasting with conventional gapped models.
main_result: A sharp, robust edge-to-edge revival is found in the two-point correlator, whose sign depends on fermion-number parity, confirming topological signatures beyond gapped superconductors.
method: Theoretical analysis using Luttinger liquid theory, particle-hole ansatz construction, and comparison with exact results from related models like the Kitaev chain.
model_or_system: The model is spinless fermions in one dimension with short-range attractive interactions, described by a Hamiltonian. It proposes realization using ultracold dipolar molecules or atoms in an optical lattice.
key_observables: Two-point correlator $\langle \hat{c}^\dagger_1 \hat{c}_j angle$, edge-to-edge revival magnitude, and the overlap $|\langle N+1|N+1angle_{	ext{ansatz}}|^2$.
important_parameters: Interaction strength $V$ (especially near $-2$), fermion number parity, and system size $L$ (analyzed in the thermodynamic limit).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes particle number conservation, which distinguishes it from standard gapped models like the Kitaev chain.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the bulk decay versus the edge revival via interferometry measurements and show how the revival persists robustly across different interaction strengths and fillings.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the model in a number-conserving framework, calculates key correlators showing the edge revival, develops an ansatz for the ground state, confirms robustness in excited states using bosonization, and concludes with an experimental protocol.
why_interesting: It bridges topological physics (Majorana modes) into gapless, interacting systems relevant to ultracold atomic setups, providing a concrete detection scheme via interferometry.

FIG. 4. (a) Revival as a function of the system size 1/L at half-filling N/L = 1/2 for strong attractive interactions V = −1.9. The revival is quantified as the maximum value of the two-point correlator ⟨ˆc† 1ˆcj⟩for j in the range [L/2, L], which corresponds to the right half of the chain. The data is fitted with a function of the form y = m/L + q, and from the fit we extract the asymptotic value q = 0.020 of the revival in the thermodynamic limit L →∞. (b) Same scaling analysis as in Fig. 4a, but for weaker attractive interactions V = −1.5. From the fit we extract the asymptotic value q = 0.013 of the revival in the thermodynamic limit.

The edge-to-edge revival is visible as a blue peak in the bottom-right and top-left corners of the ∆Cij matrices.
